newsitem.title: USA: Lawsuit challenges Tennessee incorporation law.
newsitem.headline: Lawsuit challenges Tennessee incorporation law.

text.p: City of Memphis, Tennessee Municipal League and other municipal bodies have filed a lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of a new state law that makes it easier for towns to incorporate.

The suit was filed Friday against Shelby County Election Commission, four other county election commissions, state Coordinator of Elections Brook Thompson and the State Election Commission. The plaintiffs are seeking certification as a class action.
A Davidson County chancellor was scheduled to hear arguments Monday on the plaintiffs' request for a temporary restraining order halting incorporation.

The amendment to the state's annexation law made it possible to form a municipality right outside an existing city's borders. It reduced from 1,500 to 255 the number of residents required for incorporation.

"It's probably a good thing someone filed suit because the question of legality has been hanging over this from the very start," David Lillard, a member of the Shelby County Election Commission, told the Commercial Appeal.

The plaintiffs said the new law would restrict the growth of existing cities. Some county officials said it would also siphon from county coffers a portion of sales-tax revenues that are divided among localities where the tax is collected.
Since the law took effect, petitions have been filed to incorporate four new towns in East Shelby County and others have been filed elsewhere in the state.

"Tennessee municipalities are suffering irreparable harm in that their orderly growth has been curtailed, financial security threatened and contracts with persons outside the municipal limits are impared by the application of this unconstitutional act," the lawsuit said. "These irreparable damages cannot be compensated by money damages."
